input.quote: 9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only for-cause (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and specific-trigger (9.3) termination rights, plus force-majeure termination in 27.3 and remedy-based rights in 6.2/19.4/20.5. No general Customer termination-for-convenience right exists anywhere, while Section 8.1 commits us to a three-year term with automatic 12-month renewals (8.2). Absence of a convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under the rule and fails both the preferred (30 days) and fallback (60–90 days) positions. Favourably, Vendor has no convenience right either, so the redline adds only our exit right (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no early-termination fee) and confirms Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right; 60 days' notice is available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Add a Customer termination-for-convenience right (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund) as new Section 9.4.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement runs three years with 12-month renewals but gives us no right to exit without cause, so we have added a 30 days' notice convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, consistent with our standard position. If you prefer, we can move to 60 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty, early-termination fee, or other charge, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
